If another transaction commits a login-cache invalidation between line 222 and line 236, the old results for other orgIds are cached again with a valid revision and stay stale until the next invalidation.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:381 — Cleanup is registered as `get("alias")::remove` using the literal string "alias", so none of the 21 created IdPs (idp-alias-0..20) are removed, and they leak into later tests in the realm (lines 381 and 425).

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:91 — update() gets `original` from getById(), which returns the org-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false while the org (or the realm's organizations feature) is disabled; editing a linked IdP in that state (e.g. setting hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or removing BROKER_PUBLIC) hits the "not login before or after" early return at line 405, so nothing is invalidated. After the org is re-enabled, the stale cached ID list still returns the IdP, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), so a hidden, link-only or private broker shows up on the login page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)` and uses early-returns when `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `.test(updated)` are both false (or both true with same org link). In `update()`, `original` is obtained via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, i.e. via this cached provider, not the delegate. The diff itself acknowledges IDP models may be “wrapped” (see `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` comment: “idp might have been wrapped”) and only re-checks `isEnabled()` on the returned models. Separately, the new `getForLogin()` cache path stores only internal IDs and, on cache hits, returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without re-applying `getLoginPredicate()` to filter out `hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC` changes. Therefore, if `original`/`updated` are wrappers whose `isEnabled()` (and thus `getLoginPredicate()`) is forced false due to org/feature state, an admin update that changes login-relevant flags can fall into the “both not login IDP” early return and skip invalidating the login caches, leaving stale ID lists that later surface on the login page once the wrapper stops forcing `isEnabled()` false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:236 — When a new searchKey is added, the code merges the entries of the `query` object it read at line 222 into a new entry, bumps the revision itself with invalidateObject(), and re-adds with getCurrentCounter(). If another transaction commits a login-cache invalidation between line 222 and line 236, the old results for other orgIds are cached again with a valid revision and stay stale until the next invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), when a cache entry exists but the current organizationId searchKey is not present, the code reads the existing IdentityProviderListQuery (query = cache.get(...)), then calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), then constructs a new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query) (i.e., reusing/merging the previously-read query’s other searchKey results) and re-adds it via cache.addRevisioned(..., cache.getCurrentCounter()). From the diff alone, there is no check that the previously-read query is still valid w.r.t. any invalidation that could have happened between the initial cache.get() and the re-add; thus stale per-org cached ID sets from the old query can be reintroduced into the cache under a fresh revision, matching the finding’s scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:381 — Cleanup is registered as `get("alias")::remove` using the literal string "alias", so none of the 21 created IdPs (idp-alias-0..20) are removed, and they leak into later tests in the realm (lines 381 and 425).

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:438 — The "caches are still there" checks only assertNotNull on the query entry and never compare cached contents with the actual login IdPs or check what getForLogin returns. The test also never covers the multi-searchKey merge path, a disabled org, or the login bean, so it would still pass if the cached lists were stale or never read by callers.

adjudication.rationale: The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin()` does include size assertions when initially populating caches and after invalidation (it re-runs `getForLogin` and checks `identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(...)` sizes). However, in the intermediate “caches are still there” assertions (the loops after steps 1 and 2), it only does `assertNotNull(identityProviderListQuery)` for each `FetchMode` and does not validate cached contents against current `getForLogin` results or even re-read via `getForLogin` to ensure the cache is actually used. Also, the new caching logic has a distinct merge path when the same `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` is reused with a different `searchKey` (`query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null` triggers invalidation + new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)`), but the test only queries a single `orgaId` per mode and therefore does not exercise that branch. These are concrete test-coverage gaps for the new caching behavior, but not a demonstrated product defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — Update invalidation runs getLoginPredicate on the org-aware wrapped `original` from getById (isEnabled=false when the org is disabled), but the delegate query caches on the raw DB ENABLED flag. So if an IdP in a disabled org is made hidden, link-only, non-public or disabled, the login cache is never invalidated, and the IdP shows up on the login page again once the org is re-enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `update()`, the code fetches `original` via `getById()` and passes it into `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)`. The invalidation decision relies on `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` / `.test(updated)` to decide whether to invalidate the new `getForLogin` caches. The diff shows IDP models can be "wrapped" in an organization-aware way (e.g., `getForLogin` maps through `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, and the login bean now re-checks `idp.isEnabled()` explicitly "as idp might have been wrapped"), which implies wrapper semantics can change `isEnabled`/login-availability relative to the underlying stored IDP. Meanwhile, the login caches are populated from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (raw delegate results) and store internal IDs. This creates a concrete risk that `original` is evaluated under wrapper-modified login availability (e.g., disabled due to org state), causing the early-return path (`if !pred(original) && !pred(updated) return;`) to skip invalidation even though the underlying delegate-backed cached set would be affected by the update. That mismatch can leave stale login caches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — The public SPI getLoginPredicate() now also requires BROKER_PUBLIC for org-linked IdPs, but getLoginSearchOptions(), the LoginFilter enum javadoc and the getForLogin javadoc (line 151) were not updated, so the predicate and search-options halves of the public LoginFilter API now disagree for external callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public SPI `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally filter out org-linked IDPs unless `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` parses to true (`.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(...))`). In this PR, `getLoginSearchOptions()` is not updated (no diff), and nothing in the shown changes updates any related javadoc/contract text. That creates a concrete API-contract/documentation mismatch: external callers relying on the documented LoginFilter/search-options API would not see this new implicit eligibility rule, even though it now affects results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:80 — The cached getForLogin can return org-wrapped models whose isEnabled() is false (disabled org), which contradicts the SPI javadoc promise of "enabled" login IdPs; this change patches only this caller with an isEnabled re-check instead of fixing or documenting the contract for other getForLogin consumers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a caller-side workaround in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` by adding `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() ...)` with an explicit comment that `idp` "might have been wrapped". Separately, `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)` sometimes returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (on cache miss/invalid), implying wrappers can be introduced at the SPI boundary. The finding’s broader concern—that this change addresses only one consumer rather than enforcing/documenting the SPI contract for all `getForLogin` consumers—is a concrete, diff-grounded scope/contract issue, but the diff does not conclusively prove a universal defect for all consumers or the exact javadoc guarantee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — update() runs the login predicate on the org-aware wrapper from getById, so if the IdP's org is disabled then original fails the predicate; setting hideOnLogin, linkOnly or BROKER_PUBLIC=false then skips invalidation and the stale ID stays in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL lists (the bean only re-checks isEnabled, so the IdP shows again once the org is re-enabled)

adjudication.rationale: In update(), the invalidation decision for the login caches is based on `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model)` where `idpById` comes from `getById(model.getInternalId())` and is then evaluated by `getLoginPredicate().test(original)`. This diff also shows org-aware wrapping exists (`createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` is applied in `getForLogin(...)` on cache-miss) and the UI bean explicitly notes an IdP "might have been wrapped" and therefore re-checks `isEnabled()`. If `getById(...)` returns an org-aware wrapper whose `isEnabled()` (and thus login predicate) depends on organization state, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` can incorrectly treat a login-eligible IdP as non-login (e.g., org disabled) and skip invalidation when an update changes login eligibility (hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC), leaving stale internalIds in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL lists; the cached path of `getForLogin` does not re-apply the login predicate, so stale entries would leak through (the bean only filters on `isEnabled`).

(query lookup by cache key, load current revision, delegate stream to collect internalIds, store in IdentityProviderListQuery keyed by a searchKey, then resolve each id via session.identityProviders().getById with a fallback on null). This is substantial code duplication differing mainly in cacheKey/searchKey and the delegate call, so introducing a shared helper (e.g., taking cacheKey, searchKey, and a Supplier/Function for the delegate stream) would reduce maintenance risk. However, the finding is purely a refactor/style suggestion (extract a helper) and does not describe a verifiable defect or a substantive, nontrivial review issue grounded in behavior. adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:246 — The cache stores only IdP IDs and throws away the models the delegate just loaded, so each ID is then resolved with its own getById call, which means N extra DB queries per login-page render whenever the per-IdP entries are cold or were invalidated.

On a cache hit it reconstructs results by iterating IDs and calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` for each (`for (String id : cached) { IdentityProviderModel idp = session.identityProviders().getById(id); ... }`). This can lead to N separate loads when the per-IdP entries are not already warm (even though the list cache itself is warm), which is a concrete performance concern introduced by this diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239 — The ORG_ONLY/ALL entry for each realm+mode gets one searchKey entry per organizationId with no bound, and adding each new org copies the whole previous map (O(orgs^2) total copying); in ALL mode every org's set also repeats all realm-level IdP IDs (O(orgs x realmIdPs) memory in a single never-evicted cache entry).

When a new organizationId is requested and query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, the code invalidates and then creates a new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query), which (by the call pattern) is intended to carry forward prior searchKey entries. This implies a single cache entry per realm+mode can accumulate one entry per organizationId without any bound/eviction logic shown in the diff. The claims about O(orgs^2) copying and repeated realm-level IDs depend on IdentityProviderListQuery internals (not shown), so the exact complexity can’t be fully verified from the diff, but the unbounded per-org accumulation risk is grounded in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:236 — Looking up an organizationId that is not cached yet calls invalidateObject on the shared realm+mode entry, which evicts the cached results for every other org; concurrent logins for different orgs then race on addRevisioned, lose each other's entries and keep re-querying the DB (cache thrashing, poor hit ratio).

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin()`, the cache key is shared per realm+`FetchMode` (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), not per `organizationId`. When a previously-unseen `organizationId` is requested and `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns null, the code calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` before rebuilding a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` that includes the new `searchKey`. Because the entry is shared, this invalidation evicts cached results for other org search keys under the same mode, which can reduce hit ratio and cause cache thrashing under concurrent org logins. The exact concurrency/race impact isn’t fully provable from the diff alone, but the shared-key eviction behavior is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:384 — Creating, removing or changing the login eligibility of any single IdP invalidates all three realm-wide login keys (holding every org's results) and sends cluster invalidations, so realms with frequent org/IdP provisioning get a near-zero hit ratio and re-run the full unpaginated getForLogin queries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds realm-wide caching for `getForLogin` keyed only by realm+`FetchMode` (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), while the per-organization results are stored inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` via `searchKey` (`organizationId` or ""). Invalidation on create/remove (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation`) and on certain updates (`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`) loops over `FetchMode.values()` and calls `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode))`, which clears the entire realm+mode entry, implicitly dropping cached results for *all* orgIds stored in that query. This matches the finding’s performance/scalability concern (global invalidation and re-running full `idpDelegate.getForLogin` collects). It’s not a correctness defect but a real, diff-grounded architectural/performance issue introduced by this caching design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:100 — remove() now always runs an extra idpDelegate.getByAlias DB query, even when the IdP is already in the alias cache (before this change the query only ran on the invalidated path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — original` comes from the org-aware getById wrapper, so while an org is disabled it fails the login predicate; making one of the org's IdPs private/hidden/link-only then skips invalidating the login cache, and after the org is re-enabled the stale list shows that IdP on the login page because the bean only re-checks isEnabled.

adjudication.rationale: The new `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)` can skip invalidating the new `getForLogin` caches when both `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `.test(updated)` are false (early return). But `original` is obtained via `getById()` in `update()`, and the diff explicitly notes IDPs may be “wrapped” (bean now re-checks only `isEnabled()`), implying wrapper state can affect predicate evaluation. If wrapper/state makes `original` fail the predicate (e.g., org disabled) and the update changes other login-eligibility aspects (e.g., hide-on-login/public), invalidation may be skipped. The cached path in `getForLogin()` then returns cached internal IDs without reapplying `getLoginPredicate` (it just resolves by ID), so callers that only re-check `isEnabled()` (as in the bean) could display a stale/incorrect login list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:251 — The cached path returns IdPs by cached ID without re-applying getLoginPredicate() (enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin/BROKER_PUBLIC) to the fresh models, so any missed invalidation shows non-login IdPs on the login page.

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached implementation of `getForLogin(...)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, the cached path reconstructs results by iterating cached internal IDs and fetching fresh models via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, then unconditionally adds them to the result set. It does not re-apply `getLoginPredicate()` (which now also includes the `organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC` check) or other login-eligibility filters on the fetched models. Therefore, if the cache becomes stale due to any missed/partial invalidation, the method can return IdPs that no longer qualify for login (e.g., disabled/hidden/non-public org-linked), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239 — The merge path copies the previous query's per-org results into a new entry stamped with the current revision, so an invalidation committed at the same moment can be lost and stale login IdP lists for other orgs get cached again.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin()` caching logic, when a cache entry exists but the current `organizationId` (`searchKey`) is not cached, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then rebuilds the entry with `loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)` but *also* passes the previous `query` into `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)` (the “merge” path). This effectively carries forward previously cached per-org results into a new entry that is stamped with the new/current revision (`cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`), even though those carried-forward results were computed under an older revision. That can cause stale login IdP lists for other orgs to be treated as fresh/valid until the next invalidation, matching the finding’s concern about lost/overwritten invalidations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:406 — No test queries the same mode with a second searchKey (e.g. ORG_ONLY with orgb id, or ORG_ONLY with null as the login bean does), so the merge branch (invalidateObject + new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)) is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:503 — The BROKER_PUBLIC predicate change in the SPI is only covered on an IdP with no org; there is no test that toggling BROKER_PUBLIC on an org-linked IdP invalidates the caches, or that updating a non-public org IdP leaves them alone.
